rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest call, re-checked fresh this session: chunk 3 'What You'll Learn' line 16 'Build a verifier shaped against your dominant failure (LLM judge, shell-hook, or Ralph re-feed)' -- 'Ralph re-feed' is not explained anywhere before this slide; the term is only taught via the linked lecture `what-packaging-is.md` (chunk 6) and only named in a worked example at chunk 10's 'Optional challenges' (line 91, 'Run Geoffrey Huntley's original Ralph'). Stays inside: `curriculum/vocabulary.md` line 63 registers 'verifier shapes | LLM judge · deterministic shell hook · Ralph re-feed' as a controlled training term threaded from `what-packaging-is`, and the phrase sits inside a `## What You'll Learn` LO bullet whose genre job (per `curriculum/module-shape.md`'s LO template) is to preview an outcome the module teaches later -- the reader needs only 'one of three named approaches' to follow the LO, not Ralph's definition, and the identical parenthetical (verbatim aside from a trimmed lead-in) has passed three prior slides pins unchanged. Second call: chunk 8 line 69 'the kit' -- no in-file antecedent, but `vocabulary.md` line 37 registers 'kit' as arc-earned spine vocabulary threaded from `earn-the-trust` (an earlier module), so the prior-module carve-out applies directly.

Closest call: chunk 4 'Start here' line 24 blockquote 'The M1 countermove rides along: tell the agent what output you want.' -- names the source module by its ordinal (M1) rather than by title. Stays inside: the claim is unpacked in the same sentence ('tell the agent what output you want'), matching the rule's own worked passing example ('the opening lecture's infinite chameleon: the LLM that flatters you…' -- pass); a reader does not need to know where M1 sits in the deck to follow the claim. Chunk 6's 'In the two closing lectures, the headings carry the claims' resolves in-chunk (both named lecture links follow immediately after), matching the file's own dated 'Slide deixis accepted' note for the adjacent phrase.
